definition: Hydra composes configuration for Python apps from YAML files and command-line overrides, and can sweep over many settings.
details: Created by Omry Yadan at Facebook AI Research (Meta) in 2019.

explainer.lead: How to install Hydra, a first working example, and where it fits in an AI project.
explainer.inAi: Keep many experiment settings tidy without editing code; used by many research training repos.
explainer.jsNote: Hydra is a Python library with no official JavaScript or TypeScript package; call it from a Python service if your app is written in JavaScript.

tiers.eli5: It is like a settings master file that lets you swap options from the command line and run the same program many times with different choices.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers structure configs as composable YAML groups and override values at launch, and use sweeps to run grids of experiments; the pitfall is that deeply nested composition can make it unclear which value actually wins.
tiers.paperLevel: Configurations are composed hierarchically from YAML files with command-line overrides taking precedence, supporting multirun sweeps over parameter combinations. It is a configuration framework, not a learning method; behavior depends on the precedence rules of the composition.

explainer.example: A training script reads a model config and a dataset config from YAML, and a command-line override changes the learning rate for a sweep over several values.
